author: Mets501
why: Copper and gold plates of the CUORE cryostat being assembled in a cleanroom at Italy's Gran Sasso underground laboratory: the ultra-cold detector physics that Milano-Bicocca's physicists help build.
cropNote: Square original; the 16:10 crop keeps the stacked copper plates and wiring across the frame; a gowned technician is cut off at the lower right. A small stamped label on one bracket is illegible at 480 px.

author: Udo Schröter
why: The curd for a wheel of Parmigiano Reggiano lifted from the copper vat in its linen cloth: the Po Valley dairy chain around Cattolica's Piacenza campus, from milk to protected-origin cheese.
cropNote: Landscape original; the centre crop keeps the cloth bundle and the whey-filled copper vat edge to edge. No text anywhere in frame.

author: U.S. Air Force photo by Tech. Sgt. Michael Wykes
why: A dental technician in safety glasses carving a crown in wax on a stone model of a patient's teeth: the prosthodontics half of the degree, made by hand.
cropNote: Close landscape frame; the crop keeps both hands, the wax tool and the model. Plain blue work shirt; no insignia or text in the crop.

author: M Joko Apriyo Putro
why: A pharmacist in cap, mask and gloves grinding a preparation with mortar and pestle in a compounding lab, balances and jars of ingredients around: the galenic pharmacy a pharmacist is trained to make.
cropNote: Centred subject; the crop keeps the figure, the mortar and the jars on the bench. Shelf labels behind are tiny and illegible at 480 px.

author: U.S. Geological Survey from Reston, VA, USA
why: A volcanologist in a hard hat scooping molten lava from a fresh flow into a steel bucket: sampling the Earth's interior as it reaches the surface.
cropNote: The crop keeps the stooping figure, the glowing lava tongue and the bucket among the pahoehoe folds. No text or insignia visible.

commonsFile: Gondola on the Canal Grande in Venice.jpg
author: Wolfgang Moroder
why: A gondolier rowing visitors down the Grand Canal: Venice, where Ca' Foscari sits, as a living case study in tourism and hospitality.
cropNote: Wide original; the centre crop keeps the gondola in the lower middle with the palazzi on the right. Passengers are small; no signage legible.

author: Bin im Garten
why: A ball-and-stick model of a glucose ring, red oxygens and black carbons on a dark ground: the molecular structures at the core of medicinal chemistry and drug design.
cropNote: Near-square original; the crop keeps the ring and its side groups filling the frame. No text; not a lab bench.

author: JoJan
why: A welder in a shield joining steel with a bright TIG arc at a workshop bench: making and joining metal parts, the hands-on core of mechanical engineering.
cropNote: The crop keeps the shield, the arc and the torch hand at centre; the workshop is plain behind. No logos or text visible.

author: Rob Bulmahn
why: A scale roadster in a wind tunnel with green laser streamlines tracing the air over its body: the aerodynamics work at the heart of automotive engineering in Turin, Italy's car city.
cropNote: Landscape original; the crop keeps the car body and the streamlines across the frame against a black ground. No badge or text visible at 480 px.

commonsFile: Farrier and Veterinarian at a Farm in Hardwood, Maryland on April 30, 2025 - 80.jpg
author: USDAgov
why: A vet holding a horse's muzzle to check its mouth and teeth during a farm visit: the hands-on clinical examination of large animals that veterinary medicine trains.
cropNote: The crop keeps the horse's muzzle at left and the vet's hands and face at right, in daylight. No text or logos in frame.

author: Lanoyta
why: Looking down the stacked oval tiers of the University of Padua anatomy theatre, built in 1595 so students could watch dissections from above: the medical school where Vesalius had taught anatomy half a century earlier.
cropNote: Wide original; the centre crop keeps the concentric wooden balustrades narrowing to the lit table at the bottom. Empty, no people, no text.

author: U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Christopher Toon
why: A clinician's hand steadying an otoscope in a patient's ear, its green light on: the close physical examination a doctor learns first.
cropNote: Tight close-up; the crop keeps the otoscope head, the hand and the ear. No text or insignia in frame.

author: Linda Bartlett (photographer)
why: Four doctors sharing a multi-headed teaching microscope over the same slide: how medical students learn to read tissue in pathology.
cropNote: Landscape original; the crop keeps the four faces at the eyepieces around the white microscope. Slide cabinets behind are unreadable. An older colour photograph from the US National Cancer Institute.

author: Heismadboy
why: A nurse in cap and mask taking a patient's blood pressure with a cuff and a column sphygmomanometer: the routine observations at the centre of ward nursing.
cropNote: The crop keeps the nurse at left, the cuff and gauge at centre and the masked patient at right. No text legible.

author: Jaime VD
why: Engineers in hard hats rebuilding a hydroelectric generator, its rotor lifted out and the stator coils laid round it: the power and energy plant that industrial engineers design and keep running.
cropNote: Tall original; the 16:10 centre crop keeps the red rotor shaft, the ring of coils and the small figures around it. Figures are small; no text legible at 480 px.

author: Luigi Chiesa
why: Steel distillation columns with their ladders and platforms at a chemical plant: separating and purifying substances at scale, the core unit operation of process engineering.
cropNote: Tall original; the crop keeps the cluster of columns and walkways against the sky. No signage or text visible. Distinct from Spain's petrochemical aerial.

author: Dage - Looking For Europe
why: A red jack-up platform working on MOSE, the mobile flood barrier across the Lido inlet of the Venice lagoon: hydraulic works that protect a city from the sea.
cropNote: Landscape original; the crop keeps the red platform standing in the water at centre with the shore behind. Any painted lettering on it is too small to read at 480 px.

author: Sarahhoa
why: Rows of furled beach umbrellas and sun-loungers on Rimini's shore after dark: the seaside tourism economy the Rimini campus studies, laid out in its own grid.
cropNote: Wide original; the centre crop keeps the lit umbrellas marching into the distance under a deep blue sky. No people, no text.

commonsFile: Teatro alla Scala dettaglio al lato alto del palcoscenico.jpg
author: Bramfab
why: The red curtain, gilded proscenium and stage lights at the side of La Scala's stage in Milan: one of the cultural institutions whose seasons, budgets and audiences arts managers run.
cropNote: Tall original; the 16:10 centre crop keeps the red drape at left, the gilded columns and the lighting rig. No text visible.

author: Ethan Fox Surgery
why: A gowned surgical team under the theatre lights, watching the laparoscope feed on screens as they operate: modern minimally invasive surgery in a teaching hospital.
cropNote: Landscape original; the crop keeps the team seen from behind, the lamps above and the two monitors. The monitor images are small and not graphic at 480 px; no text legible.

author: USCapitol
why: Masons in hard hats on a scaffold repointing the joints of a stone facade: the repair and upkeep of existing buildings, a large part of building engineering in historic cities such as Ravenna.
cropNote: Landscape original; the crop keeps the mason's trowel on the stone joint, a second mason and an onlooker on the scaffold. No logos or text legible.

author: Rob Bulmahn
why: A silicon wafer of integrated circuits breaking light into a rainbow across its rows of dies: the chips that electronic and communications engineers design.
cropNote: Landscape close-up; the crop fills the frame with the grid of dies in a red-to-violet sweep. No text; abstract but recognisably a chip wafer.

commonsFile: Entrance to the Cave of the Sibyl, Cumae (8138833365).jpg
author: Carole Raddato
why: The trapezoidal rock-cut gallery known as the Cave of the Sibyl at Cumae, near Naples, the setting Virgil gave the Sibyl in the Aeneid: the ancient texts of classics made into a place.
cropNote: Tall original; the 16:10 centre crop keeps the stepped trapezoid openings receding down the lit tunnel. No people, no text.

commonsFile: Sonography Machine Donation from Raleigh Radiology-14.jpg
author: waketechcc
why: A student in scrubs and gloves scanning a classmate's neck with an ultrasound probe in a clinical skills lab: learning point-of-care imaging hands-on.
cropNote: Landscape original; the crop keeps the student, the probe on the neck and the scanner at right. Faces of the lying volunteer and a man in the background are small; no text legible at 480 px.

commonsFile: Mosquito trap to study avian malaria in Himalayas JEG0168.jpg
author: PJeganathan
why: A field biologist hanging a mosquito trap in forest undergrowth to sample disease-carrying insects: tracking how pathogens move between the environment, animals and people.
cropNote: Landscape original; the crop keeps the trap at centre-left and the researcher's hands and profile at right among leaves. No text or logos visible.

author: cudmore
why: Culture bottles of fruit flies on a lab shelf, each a genetic line kept alive for crosses: Drosophila, the organism that taught genetics most of what it knows about genomes.
cropNote: Landscape original; the crop keeps the row of cotton-stoppered bottles with flies and food at the base. A small handwritten mark on one bottle is illegible at 480 px. Not a bench with a person pipetting.

author: Kristina Walter
why: A hand placing a figure in a sand tray among toy animals and trees during sandplay: a therapy method where a client builds a scene that the psychologist then helps interpret.
cropNote: Landscape original; the crop keeps the raked sand, the animal figures and the adult hand at top right. No faces, no text.

author: Melirius
why: The three-kilometre arm of the Virgo gravitational-wave detector at Cascina, near Pisa, running straight to the horizon: precision physics built as engineering.
cropNote: Landscape original; the crop keeps the blue arm tube receding down the centre between service roads and fields. No people; no text.

author: Metropolitan Transportation Authority of the State of New York
why: A tunnel worker beside the cutterhead of a tunnel boring machine as it breaks through into a rock cavern: underground construction, where civil engineers plan metro lines and road tunnels.
cropNote: Landscape original; the crop keeps the disc cutters of the machine face at left and the worker in a hard hat at right against wet rock. No logos or text legible at 480 px.

commonsFile: Blood draw procedure at the laboratory at UCLA Medical Plaza.jpg
author: Jengod
why: A gloved hand drawing blood from a patient's arm into a collection tube: one of the first hands-on clinical skills a medical student practises.
cropNote: Tall original; the 16:10 centre crop keeps the gloved hand, the tube with its blood and the outstretched arm against a pale wall. No faces; any tube label is too small to read at 480 px.

commonsFile: 20230630 Structure of Katajanokan Laituri - Helsinki, Suomi, Finland.jpg
author: Aarni Salomaa
why: The glulam columns and cross-laminated timber floors of a new building going up in Helsinki: low-carbon timber construction, the material shift that sustainable building engineering designs for.
cropNote: Landscape original; the crop keeps the timber columns, beams and floor slabs under the steel roof frame. Wrapped material packs along the bottom edge carry printed patterns but no legible words at 480 px. No people.
